title: Checklist

lessons.title: Course Material: Checklist.pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Packaging & Pricing Your Services – Cheat Sheet  Introduction ü Packaging up services is a great way to meet client needs and grow your business ü When you work hard to attract new clients you want to make sure that you keep them  ü Packaging can help you make more sales and keep your clients for longer ü Offer a range of packages so clients can choose depending on their needs and their budget ü You need to be absolutely clear on what’s included and what the outcomes will be ü Here is your roadmap through the course:           Identify Current Profitable Services & ClientsPinpoint Client NeedsOutline Package IdeasEstimate Price & Check ProfitabilityTest Package IdeasDetail Your PackagesDraft Package Creation PlanOutline Sales Materials and Marketing Plan

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  Learning Objectives:  ü Identify where service packages fit into your existing business and how they will increase your sales ü Delve into your ideal clients’ needs, so that you are clear on the solutions your packages must address ü Select the package type you’ll offer that will most effectively meet the needs of your clients ü Decide on your initial pricing, so that you can present a range of price points for different clients’ budgets ü Estimate the profitability of your package ideas, so that you can be sure they will increase your income and grow your business ü Determine how your packages increase the lifetime value of a client and then validate your ideas, so that you’re confident you can sell your packages ü Pick your “best value” or “most popular” package and identify how your other packages fit together, so that you can offer an optimal number of choices that maximize your sales ü Detail the contents of each package and draft a package creation plan, so that you can immediately take action to create the packages that will work for your business ü Plan what sales and marketing materials you’ll need to promote your first packages and scale your revenue quickly  ü Outline a marketing plan and create a timeline for marketing your priority package ü Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps, so that you can achieve the goals you set for this course and develop further

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Overview of the 4-Step Process to Package your Services  ü 4 steps to easily package up and promote your services: 1. Identify Your Clients’ Needs 2. Upgrade Your Business Model with Packages  3. Outline Your Package Creation Plan 4. Create Your Package Marketing Plan   ü We’ve provided a Service Package Planner & Tracker spreadsheet to complete during the course  ü You can also use the relevant space in the Action Guide to do your planning  ü Choose whichever method works best for you   Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  Module 1 - How Offering Packages Will Increase Your Sales    Key Takeaways: Ø Packages focus on providing the solutions your clients are looking for. Ø Packaging is a great way to plan out business growth.  Learning Objective: ü Identify where service packages fit into your existing business and how they will increase your sales  What is a Package? ü A package is a collection of services offered at different price points to give clients choices ü Packages work well for service-based businesses that o currently offer a random selection of services,  o or even just one type of service and one current package ü It’s a way to consolidate existing offers and add on new ones ü Packages focus on providing the solution your clients are looking for ü Some different ways to package up your services: o Different tiers of service at different price points. E.g., Bronze, Silver, and Gold levels of service   o Block of pre-booked sessions or a retainer, e.g., A package of 12 yoga sessions or a year’s retainer of coaching services o Task-focused packages which offer solutions to specific tasks,

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  e.g., an email management package or a social media marketing package  Where Do Packages Fit into a Business Model?  ü You can package up your services no matter what business model you have:  o One-on-one coaching services to private individuals  o Membership businesses  o Consultancy services     o Regular services to clients such as hairdressing, sports coaching, or health care  Your Business Model ü Think about whether a different model would make sense for you to grow into  ü How do you think your business would benefit from packages?  ü Advantages to your business o Clarify service offers o Save time customizing standard services for each client o Increase reach o Generate more revenue o Get better results for clients o Forecast income  o Introduce upselling ü Advantages for clients  o Wider choice (level and price) o Increased value

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  o Access to more of what they need o Better results  o Easier to find the right solution ü Start to create packages using what you do now: o Services that potential clients ask you for time and time again   o services you’re currently doing on a repetitive basis for clients   Your Highest Profits ü Figure out where you currently get your highest profits ü Look back at your past year’s sales figures  ü Look at how much time you and your team spend on different current offers  ü Pinpoint the top 3 services that generated the most profit and identify the most profitable of all.  ü List your most profitable services  ü You might offer packages with a smaller profit margin which sell in volume ü Identify which 3 services bring you the most revenue and pinpoint the one most revenue-generating of the 3  ü Identify the reasons people have given for their purchases up to now o Find comments they’ve given you in testimonials, on social media, in emails, in conversations

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7   Action Steps: 1. What is your current business model? Write this down, and note what model makes sense for you to grow into. 2. Write down how your business would benefit from packages and how your clients would benefit.  3. Research where your main profits currently come from.  a. Note the top three that generated the most profit and identify the most profitable of all. b. Identify which three services bring you the most revenue and pinpoint the most revenue-generating of the three.  c. Add this information to the Services tab of your Service Package Planner & Tracker. 4. Refer back to any comments you’ve received showing what needs are being met from your current services. a. Add this information for each of your identified services on the Services tab of your Service Package Planner & Tracker.

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Module 2 – Step 1:  Identify Your Clients’ Needs  Key Takeaways: Ø You must understand your clients’ challenges and needs if you want to create packages that solve their problems. Ø It’s crucial to find out where your clients are in their businesses or their lives as this will influence the solutions you propose  Learning Objective: ü Delve into your ideal clients’ needs, so that you are clear on the solutions your packages must address  Identify Your Most Profitable Client  ü Who do you want to target with your packages? ü Who already spends the most with you?  The 80/20 Rule ü 80/20 (Pareto Principle): 80% of sales come from about 20% of clients ü Use it as a rough guide to help identify your most profitable clients   1. Look at your total sales for last year/last quarter     2. Run a report of total sales by each client 3. Identify those who spent most with you ü Don’t neglect the other 80%. They’re still important

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  ü Most people find that this top 20% are their ideal clients ü Write down a description of this client  ü Find information about these clients from your records   Your Clients’ Level of Experience ü Find out where your clients are in their businesses or their lives ü This will influence the solutions you propose  ü Look at what you know about your profitable clients and divide them into: o Starter - they’re starting out or have basic needs, e.g., first time start-up, new to marketing or tech, looking for their first corporate job  o Intermediate – they’re already part way through a journey but have got stuck, e.g., they have some clients but can’t grow beyond that   o Advanced – those with an established service business but who want to keep scaling and growing  Drill Down to Client Needs ü You must know what your clients’ needs are  ü Your packages will be solutions-based ü Each element in them should be included with an outcome in mind ü Arrange conversations to pinpoint the greatest needs of those clients   ü Try to call at least 5 or 6 people to give you a representative sample ü Explain you need their help ü Have a 30- or 45-minute phone or video conference call ü Record these conversations, if they agree

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  ü Start by reviewing their experience with you: o What did you most appreciate about the service? o What would you have liked less/more of? ü Other questions you need answers to: 1. What’s your number one challenge at the moment? 2. When you’re trying to solve a problem, how do you get your best results? (e.g. video, self-study, one-on-one) 3. What fits in best with your lifestyle? (e.g. evening/weekend working) 4. Is there anything you need that I’m not currently offering?  5. Do you buy XX services from anyone else?  6. What’s the most important thing to you when you invest in a service? (e.g. reliability, speed, convenience, professionalism) 7.
